title: CRLR/74/2012 of NEERAJ BHARDWAJ @ RAM BHARDWAJ Vs VIDHI BHARDWAJ

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 74 of 2012
Neeraj Bhardwaj. ÖÖ.Revisionist.
Versus
Vidhi Bhardwaj. Ö......Ö. Respondent.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the respondent.
When revision was taken up in the pre-lunch
session, Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate, made statement at bar
that he has received telephonic instructions from his client that
his client would deposit ` 5000/- in his account to enable him
to make payment of ` 5,000/- to respondent Vidhi Bhardwaj in
compliance of order dated 13.05.2013, therefore, matter may be
posted after lunch.
This Court on 13.05.2013 passed following order:
ìMr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the
respondent.
To resolve the matrimonial dispute, serious
efforts should be made; therefore, parties are
directed to remain present in person before
this Court on 31.05.2013. Revisionist /
husband shall pay ` 5,000/- to the wife
enabling her to come to this Court on the
date fixed.î

2
On 31.05.2013, this case was adjourned for today
with the direction that parties shall remain present before this
Court to explore the possibility of mutual settlement.
Respondent Vidhi Bhardwaj is present, in person, and is duly
identified by her counsel but revisionist is not present.
When the matter is taken up in post lunch session,
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate stated that his client has placed
him in a embarrassing position in view of the fact that amount,
promised to be deposited in the morning, has not been
deposited and despite his repeated efforts, he was not able to
get in contact with the revisionist telephonically, therefore, he is
not representing him any more.
This revision is filed challenging the order dated
14.10.2011 passed by Judge, Family Court, Haridwar in Misc.
Case No. 164 of 2007 whereby revisionist was directed to pay
maintenance @ ` 5000/- per month to the respondent. It has
further been held by the Family Court that revisionist has
shown his income as ` 15,000/- per month at the time when
talks of marriage were going on. It has further been observed
by the trial court that ` 5,000/- per month would be sufficient
amount to maintain respondent wife.
It has been reported by Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate
for the respondent that despite passing of impugned order,
revisionist is not paying any amount to the respondent.
Having perused the entire material available on
record, I do not find any ambiguity or jurisdictional error in the
impugned judgment. Therefore, revision fails and is dismissed.
However, it is directed that revisionist shall pay entire arrears
from the date of filing of application under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
within 15 days from today along with ` 5,000/-, as directed by

3
this Court vide order dated 13.05.2013, failing which trial court
will be at liberty to proceed against the revisionist in
accordance with law to ensure the recovery from the
revisionist.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 02.07.2013
SKS
